/Issued 509 AM MDT Tue Sep 1 2026/ 

 - Meteorological Overview:

Longwave troughing over the Western CONUS, with south to southwest 
flow aloft across the Northern Rockies, will dominate the upcoming 
week. Shortwaves ejecting from the base of the trough axis and 
lifting north to northeast within the aforementioned flow regime 
will bring multiple opportunities for showers and thunderstorms to 
Southwest through North Central Montana, most notably today and 
Wednesday when the areal coverage precipitation will be greatest. 
High temperatures, with the exception of today when highs will 
generally be 5 to 10 degrees above normal, will mostly range from 
near to below normal. Periods of strong and gusty winds will occur 
over the next week, especially on Wednesday and Thursday within the 
north-south orientated valleys of Southwest Montana where frequent 
gusts in excess of 45 mph are likely to occur. - Moldan

- Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

Strong Winds on Wednesday and Thursday...

ECMWF EFIs with respect to winds continue to support the potential 
for an unusual to very unusual wind event, for early September, 
through the period along and south of the I-90 corridor; most 
notably within the Madison River Valley. Southerly H700 winds per 
NAEFS analysis across Southwest Montana are prog'd to increase to 
between 30-40kts by 18z Wednesday, and remain so through 00z Friday 
before decreasing. These 2 to 2.5 standard deviation wind speeds 
aligned with the north-south terrain in Southwest Montana, 
specifically the Madison River Valley, combined with deep mixing 
between 16z to 02z each day will support an ideal scenario for an 
early season High Wind event. Given that NBM5.0 probabilities within 
the Madison River for sustained wind speeds to exceed 40 mph range 
between a 60-70% chance (Wednesday) and 30-40% chance (Thursday), 
confidence remains high enough to continue the High Wind Watch with 
this forecast package. The main reason for not upgrading the High 
Wind Watch was uncertainty with respect to Wednesday night's into 
Thursday's winds, which at this point in time appear to be slightly 
weaker than during the daylight hours on Wednesday. Additionally, I 
was unable to find a (6-9 hour) period in which wind speeds and/or 
gusts decrease significantly enough in order to break-up the event 
into two (2) distinct wind events, thus the watch from 18z Wednesday 
through 03z Friday remains in effect for the Madison River Valley.

Severe Thunderstorm Risk for Wednesday...

A marginal risk for severe thunderstorms, mainly capable of 
producing damaging winds, exists on Wednesday along and northwest of 
a Helena, to Monarch, to Winifred line. Showers and thunderstorms 
lifting northeast from Idaho and Western Montana are expected to 
overspread the aforementioned area through the afternoon hours, with 
BUFKIT sounding depicting inverted-V's beneath cloud bases of 
10000kft. These high cloud bases combined with already anomalous low 
level wind speeds will support the potential for a few severe 
thunderstorm/shower wind gusts across portions of Central and North 
Central Montana. - Moldan
